subject: problem comparing analyses with relyonsleeplog = TRUE/FALSE

messages.author: 1c8682eea45d1330
messages.subject: problem comparing analyses with relyonsleeplog = TRUE/FALSE
parts:
Hi all,

I have successfully analysed 14 nights of sleep for 6 participants in GGIR.

Participants have filled out a sleep diary and using relyonsleeplog = TRUE I get the following results for sleep duration:

id night_number dur_nightsleep_min_T0_yesdiary
15 2 385
15 3 469.75
15 4 421.4167
15 5 409.0833
15 6 392.1667
15 7 378.25
15 8 429.5
15 9 371.5
15 10 446.9167
15 11 367.6667
15 12 428.9167
15 13 399.4167

I would like to compare the GGIR analysis on the same data using relyonsleeplog = FALSE, to test if maybe we can ditch the sleep diary (which participants find cumbersome). For this analysis I get the following results:

id night_number dur_nightsleep_min_T0_nodiary
15 2 387
15 3 481.25
15 4 426.0833
15 5 411.4167
15 6 413.8333
15 7 388.5
15 8 440.75
15 9 381.3333
15 10 0
15 11
15 12
15 13
15 14

As you can see, the analysis using no sleep diary does not result in estimates beyound night #9. This is repeated in the results for the other 5 participants as well.

MY QUESTION IS: do I need to change other parameters, beyond  relyonsleeplog = TRUE=>FALSE, to make GGIR analyse more than 9 nights of sleep with no sleep log?

Best regards, Morten


P.S: Here is my GGIR script:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),

             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= "E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/4. Sleeplog_CSV-file/Gruppe 2019-04_t3/Gruppe 2019-04_t3.csv",
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE, #TRUE visualises only nights with a difference between sleeplog and sustained inactivity, FALSE visualises all nights
             nnights = 14,
             idloc=2, # id number drawn from: 1=file header, 2=numbers before the underscore in the filename
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------

             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] problem comparing analyses with relyonsleeplog = TRUE/FALSE
parts:
Hi Morten,
 relyonsleeplog = FALSE, does make your analysis not depend on the sleeplog. It has a different function (see tutorial).

You should do the following instead:
loglocation = c(),
def.noc.sleep=c(1),

Vincent

Thank you, Vincent! I tried your suggestions and they worked like a charm. Preliminary correlations and scatterplots of results with/without sleep diary look very promising now. I managed to get the problem of not analyzing beyond night #9 corrected, by specifying ”maxdur=0“ (was “maxdur=9”).

Thanks again - best regards, Morten
